texts: Retrograde cardioplegia is delivered backwards through the coronary sinus, and it can be given simultaneously with antegrade cardioplegia: D is the answer.
It reaches muscle beyond blocked arteries, but it perfuses the right ventricle and septum poorly, so it does not perfuse the same areas as antegrade delivery.
The catheter is usually placed blindly through the right atrium, without bicaval cannulation, and it has proven clinical benefit.
Memory hook: Sanji pours from the crown while Zoro pushes from the sink, both at the same moment.
